lines: I spiked three harbour stories this week and I will spike a fourth.
Not because they are wrong. Because three sources with the same rumour
is one rumour. Bring me a document and I will put it on the front page.
Births, deaths, notices, and lost Kin. A penny a line except the last one.
Lost Kin has been free since 1011 and nobody has ever proposed changing it,
which for a newspaper is close to a miracle.
Three months on the same thing. Deep hulls chartered and left at moorings.
Money that goes round four companies and comes out somewhere respectable.
I have everything except one piece of paper with a name on it.
Forty thousand before dawn and I set every letter of it backwards.
You get to reading the world the wrong way round. It is a hazard.
The good news is you notice when a sentence has been changed after it was set.
Eleven pins on that map. Twenty-two districts.
I do four of the districts with no pins and I see everything
and nobody has ever once asked me a single question about any of it.
A DOG, APPARENTLY. That is a headline. In a capital city.
I have written to them nine times. They print every letter.
That is the infuriating part. They print every single one.
